cli.smoke.test.shim smoke: A RE-JOIN IN PLACE UNDER THE INTERPOSER (decision 0003 §BS) — B JOINED with `-o interception`; two processes under LD_PRELOAD hold ring sessions on B: a `dd` WRITER fed through a FIFO overwriting `own/w` (1 MiB, written before; `conv=notrunc,fsync`) — 8 × 64 KiB before the eviction — and a `dd` READER of `own/r` (1 MiB) stalled on a full pipe after its first blocks → B idle-clean (syncfs), its beat held past T_owner, A evicts and recovers it → B RE-JOINS IN PLACE → both processes carry on through the SAME sessions, no error surfacing: 8 more blocks written and fsync'd, the reader drains the rest — both exit 0, every byte equal (`own/w` on A = the 16 blocks fed; the reader's stream = `own/r`), the ring served the post-re-join ops (`ipc_ops_write`/`ipc_ops_read` grew on B, the session count unchanged) → umount B, A (exit 0), fsck clean

cli.smoke.test.smoke: --daemon --supervise --log-file: the invoking process returns 0 only after ready, the log file is 0600 and carries the ready line, umount ends the daemon and the supervisor; a refused daemon mount reports its reason to the invoker

cli.smoke.test.smoke: 1,100 CONCURRENT WRITES, FSYNCS AND O_DIRECT READS ON ONE MOUNT OVER A SLOW DEVICE NEVER ANSWER EAGAIN (decision 0003 §BO's law, the data plane's half) — a set over device-mapper slices, every write and flush 5 ms late (dm-delay) → 1,100 threads (past the transport's 1,024 handler slots) each create a file, then at one gate write 64 KiB into it, at the next fsync it (1,100 promotions into packs at once: their DMAs and barriers on the data lanes), at the last read 48 KiB of it O_DIRECT off the page grain (the packed tenant's window through the bounce pool): every op answers 0 — never EAGAIN — and every read is byte-equal; the lanes' free-cell door and the bounce pools' exhaustion reported (their bounds keep this venue below them: the lane depth 4,096 > the handler slots; the ranged slab ≥ 2,048) → umount clean

cli.smoke.test.smoke: 300 CONCURRENT FSYNCS AND 300 CONCURRENT CREATES ON ONE MOUNT NEVER ANSWER EAGAIN (0003 §BO) — a set over device-mapper slices, mount A (the manager) + B JOINED: B's journal lane and conveyor are the floor ring's (64 request cells, 128 queue cells: the bounds that answered EAGAIN before §BO) → the device made a slow one (dm-delay: every write and flush 5 ms later) → 300 threads each `mkdir` a directory in B's own `s`, then at one gate create a file in it (300 parents: 300 creates at the daemon at once), then at a second gate fsync the directory (the metadata barrier) and the file: every op answers 0 — never EAGAIN — inside the row's bound, with more than 64 fsyncs held on B's lane at once; B's must-stay-0 gauges 0 → the working table back → umount B, umount A

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A BIND OF THE MOUNT IS THE KERNEL'S, NEVER THE DAEMON'S TO STOP (xfstests generic/409–411, 589 under the symmetric default) — mount, `mount --bind` it elsewhere, a file written through the mount reads through the bind; (a) the kernel's `umount` of the original: the daemon is not signalled, the bind KEEPS SERVING (`.stats`, the file sha-equal), `umount` of the bind drops the superblock's last reference and the daemon exits within two ticks, exit 0; (b) `squeezefs umount <bind>`: the kernel's plain detach naming daemon and mount, nothing signalled, the mount serves on; (c) `squeezefs umount <mount>` with the bind alive: the orderly stop ends its connection AT ONCE naming the bind (red: 30 s of `residency backstop lapsed` ×N groups), the bind answers ENOTCONN and detaches plainly; (d) generic/410's breakage — a tmpfs stacked INSIDE the tree (on the manager's dentry `sub`) stands through a member's join and through the member's changes of the shared root (fsstress's `fss<pid>` temp names, a directory renamed into and removed): the walk through `sub` reads the tmpfs each time, the join's whole-view epoch withheld (red on dev: that INC_EPOCH made `sub` invalid at the next walk and the kernel's `d_invalidate` detached the tmpfs — `sub/x` ENOENT); (e) a copy propagation made of the mount (its parent shared with a peer) goes WITH the orderly unmount — never another mount: no `other mount(s) of this superblock`, no abort, exit 0, nothing of ours left at the peer (red on dev: the verdict, read before the umount2, counted the copy and aborted under it); fsck --offline --scrub 0 findings after each

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A CLOSE BURST COALESCES ITS DRAINS (decision 0003 §AF) — no-open, no write cache: `log` written past inline (its close drains), then a shell holds it open for append and 200 forked `/bin/echo` children write a line each through it — every child's exit closes its copy, a FLUSH with custody ⇒ ONE drains (the first), the rest defer to the reclaim cadence's next tick (drains ≤ 2 + the windows the burst spanned, drains + deferred ≥ 200; drained each, they re-uploaded a whole block per close: 57,000× amplification measured) → the deferred custody lands (owed 0, parked 0) → kill -9 → fsck --offline clean → remount → every line there

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A DAEMON ENDS ONLY THE CONNECTION IT OWNS (decision 0003 §AN, §S) — mount A → `kill -TERM` A, its teardown HELD right after its own umount2 (the seam: the kernel destroyed A's superblock and reissues its connection id) → every anonymous-device number below A's is filled with a tmpfs so a FRESH mount B (its own volume, A's mountpoint) is given A's id → B ready and serving → A released: A's teardown touches nothing (no `other mount(s) of this superblock`, no fusectl abort), B serves on, A exits 0, B's orderly umount exits 0 (red on 1fcef90: A's end-if-held verdict read the table AFTER its unmount, matched B's mount by the reissued `major:minor` and aborted B's connection — gate 94: shard 1/16's daemon ended shard 8/16's fresh connection 115 inside its INIT, `the INIT reply write returned -2`)

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A DEAD MANAGER HOLDING A STRIPED HOT DIRECTORY (rung 10 recovery item 6) — A (the manager) mkdirs `hot` and flips it over K = 64 stripes (the explicit command: A holds the map and every stripe); B JOINED storms creates into it (every one shipped to A, keyed to its stripe) → kill -9 A mid-storm ⇒ B PARKS at T_self (park expiries 0) → remount A (the D0 ladder's same-host successor, term 2; its mount replays its own region — the map, the stripes, the shipped inserts) → B's reclaim lands in the grace window, the storm resumes into the same stripes → `ls` = `find` and the stat digest equal from A and B, every counted name listed → umount B, A → fsck --offline --scrub 0 findings (C17 clean)

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A FAILED REPLAY'S JOURNAL TAIL IS HELD, NEVER DISCARDED (charter §5.2, decision 0003 §BR) — a `--daemon --supervise` set over one device-mapper device, under the landing-hold seam, acks creates whose journal writes never issue; the table flips to `error`; kill -9: the supervisor's replay FAILS and the tail is HELD (its copy under the held dir before the guard drops); (a) the supervisor alive, the table restored: its retry lands the tail, removes the copy and exits — the next mount reads every acked create; (b) the supervisor KILLED with the tail held: the copy stays, the table restored, the next mount replays it before it admits writes (`held_tail_replays` 1) — every acked create present, the copy gone; fsck clean after each (red on 885727b: `replay FAILED (…) — acked metadata of the flush window may be lost`, the tail discarded, the creates gone after the device recovered)

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A FAILED VOLUME'S DAEMON SERVES EIO UNTIL ITS UNMOUNT AND NEVER DIES OF IT — ITS UNMOUNT ALWAYS COMPLETES AND NEVER LEAVES A SERVER-LESS MOUNT (xfstests generic/753; charter §1.8) — a set over a device-mapper device whose table flips to `error` without lockfs under an xattr storm, 8 cycles: the volume latches FAILED (a create answers EIO), the daemon stays alive with its mount in the table; the storm killed, `squeezefs umount` exits 0 without the `no squeezefs daemon serves it` fallback, the daemon exits 1 by itself naming the FAILED member (its supervisor: `exited (wait status 0x100)` — never a signal), no mount at the path, a second `squeezefs umount` answers `not mounted`; the working table back, the next mount serves the storm's tree, unmounts clean and the set fscks clean; once a volume latched FAILED each per-operation failure class (window write, hole cover, node read, bset append, checkpoint tick, …) logs at most ONE line until the exit, the rest counted (red on 517121d: up to 226 window-write, 231 hole and 210 bset-append lines after the latch in one cycle) — the data plane's classes too, under a cache-less data storm beside it (fsync and syncfs legs, in-place DMAs, edge seed reads, lost staged reads, block-map commits); a cycle whose volume never latches logs ONE node-read line per read-failure episode (red on 5d3e411: 11,463 in-place DMA lines after the latch in one cycle, 5,910 node-read lines in the never-latched one) (red on 7a6e224: every failed node read freed its 256 KiB buffer twice — the second munmap took a FUSE worker's live listxattr array, SIGSEGV, wait status 0x8b, the test's unmount met a mount with no daemon)

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A FOREIGN BLOCK MAP THE TOKEN CANNOT SERVE ANSWERS EIO, NEVER ZEROS — mount A (the manager) + B JOINED under SQUEEZEFS_TEST_FOREIGN_MAP_FAIL (every block-map window B resolves off A's token fails), no write cache, 512 KiB blocks under 64 KiB nodes → A writes `k/big` (192 MiB: tree-mapped) → B's read of `big` answers EIO (red before: it read zeros, sha-unequal, rc 0) and B's write into the middle of `big` answers EIO with nothing published (red before: it seeded its block from the fabricated hole and A's file lost the block's other bytes) → A's `big` sha-equal to what A wrote; umount B, A → fsck --offline --scrub 0 findings

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A FREED BLOCK IS NOT REUSED BEFORE THE RECORD THAT FREED IT IS DURABLE (charter §6.2 block reclaim, §5.2 the ack point; decision 0003 §BT) — a --single-writer set (the flat allocator: a mint takes the free list first) over device-mapper slices, cache-less: three one-block files of 0xa1, 0xa2, 0xa3 written O_DIRECT, fsync'd and synced, eight empty files beside them; the metadata slice slowed 12 s (dm-delay on writes and flushes: every journal window and barrier issued from here is in flight, as one inside the ≤ 50 ms flush span is); `fpunch 0 4m` of the second (answered once its window landed — its barrier still in flight), then `truncate 0` of the first and `rm` of the third (each answered at its RAM apply), then eight O_DIRECT one-block writes of 0xbb; the power cut inside the delay (dm-flakey drop_writes, kill -9 of the foreground daemon: no supervisor, no tail replay), the slices back: the three freed blocks still hold 0xa1, 0xa2, 0xa3 on the device — none was written, nor discarded, before its record was durable; fsck --offline --scrub clean; after the remount the truncate and the unlink were never durable and the two files read their OWN bytes, the landed punch reads its hole (red on 2d44c33: the frees ran right after the answer, the writers' mints took the freed blocks off the free list — the truncated file read 4 MiB of 0xbb, the unlinked one zeros: its block discarded by the debt drainer; fsck found nothing)

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A FULL DATA STORE ANSWERS ENOSPC — NEVER EIO — AT write(2) AND AT THE SYNC POINT, ONE LINE PER EPISODE (charter §8's terminal law, the sync point's half) — two 192 MiB data volumes of 1 MiB blocks, the write cache ON: 100 KiB files written (never synced) until write(2) refuses — the residents' claim on the store (`statfs` free counts it) covers the free blocks, `df` shows under one block free, every refusal says 'No space left on device' → `sync -f` promotes the residents into packs until the store has no block for the rest: exit 1 with ENOSPC, the daemon's ONE 'data store FULL' warning, no error line, no tripwire, fsync_promote_enospc ≥ 1 → fsync of every file: the kept ones answer ENOSPC (the same episode: still one line) and are removed → `sync -f` exits 0 → ten tenants of one pack removed: their block returns, a fresh file lands, the episode closes with its tally → kill -9 → fsck --offline clean → remount → every surviving file byte-equal to the pattern (red on dev: 'Input/output error' from `sync -f` and from dd's fsync, 'syncfs: a leg failed (InputOutput)' and 'fsync ino N: a leg failed (InputOutput)' per sync point — generic/750: 235 + 79 in 19 s; the write cache admitted every byte and the dismount pass FAILED 1,481 residents)

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A HOLDER'S TRUNCATE BETWEEN A JOINER'S PUBLISH AND ITS CLAIM WINS — A (the manager) + B JOINED under SQUEEZEFS_TEST_FOREIGN_CLAIM_HOLD, no write cache: A holds `own/f` (6 MiB, synced); B writes 4 KiB at 5 MiB and parks between its publish and its size claim; A truncates `f` to 1 MiB; B's claim then lands — the truncate wins: `f` is 1 MiB on both mounts and A's first MiB byte-exact (red before: `max(size, claim)` regrew it to 5 MiB + 4 KiB over the clipped block and A's truncated tail); a truncate-up to 6 MiB reads zeros past the cut; fsck --offline --scrub 0 findings

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A JOINED MEMBER READS A HOLDER'S BLOCK-MAP FILE, AND ITS RECALL PURGES THE BLOCKS THAT FILE MAPS, NEVER THE PEER'S WHOLE CACHE — mount A (the manager) + B JOINED, no write cache, 512 KiB blocks under 64 KiB nodes → A writes `k/big` (192 MiB: tree-mapped, `kvmap_crossings` 1) and `k/x` (4 MiB) → B reads `big` sha-equal to A's (its bindings off the map window A's token carries — red before: B resolved them off its own view of A's tree and read ZEROS) and reads both until its tiers serve them → A appends 1 MiB to `big` → B's recall of `big` purges the blocks it resolved under the token and runs no census (`dlm_token_recall_census_purges` + 0, purged keys ≥ 384): B's next read of `x` is served from its tiers, its next read of `big` reads from the device and is A's bytes, the appended MiB included

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A JOINED MEMBER'S APPEND TO ANOTHER MEMBER'S FILE IS READ BACK BYTE-EXACT — foreground (no write cache, decision 0003 §BR.6): the same eight files and the same writes from B — every file byte-exact against the mirror through B and through A at once, and again after both remount; fsck --offline --scrub 0 findings

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A JOINED MEMBER'S APPEND TO ANOTHER MEMBER'S FILE IS READ BACK BYTE-EXACT — supervised (the write cache): A (the manager) writes eight files in its own slot (a 1 MiB, a 1,000 B inline, a 5 MiB striped, a 3 MiB, a 1 MiB, a 4 MiB − 10 B — synced — and a 100 KiB and a 5 MiB + 2,616 B never synced) and reads them; B JOINED appends (`echo >>`, `cat >>` past the inline bound, across a block boundary, onto both unsynced files), writes past EOF (a gap), in the middle (unaligned and aligned) and after a truncate-up — every file byte-exact against a mirror through B and through A at once, and again after both remount; fsck --offline --scrub 0 findings

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A JOINED PEER READS THE HOLDER'S UNLANDED WRITES (charter §5.5 tokens, §6.2 the write-back drain, §AL.5; the cache-less posture of every unsupervised mount, decision 0003 §BR.6) — mount A (the manager) and B (joined), both FOREGROUND (no supervisor, so no write cache; every TTL class at 60 s): A writes 3 MB and closes ⇒ B stats it 3,000,000 and reads it byte-exact; A writes a second 3 MB file and HOLDS its fd open ⇒ B reads it exact; A truncates the second to 1 MB ⇒ B reads 1,000,000 exact; A rewrites the first with `>` (O_TRUNC) to 2 MB ⇒ B reads 2,000,000 exact; B writes 3 MB ⇒ A reads it exact. B's first read of each size is the verdict, never a value waited out until the holder's write-back drain lands it (red before: B stat'ed 0 for A's fresh 3 MB file — the grant carried the DURABLE size while A's parked write custody and its size claim had not landed)

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A JOINER'S CLEAN UNMOUNT AND REJOIN while the manager stays up — mount A (the manager) → B JOINED writes inline, staged and striped files (sha list) → `umount` B (clean: every lease released, the page Free, every staged file promoted; A reads every file sha-equal) → B mounts again at the same mount point: JOINED as appender 1 again (its projection's rows naming appender 1 are a previous incarnation's — loaded unleased), every file of every cycle sha-equal on B, B writes more; three cycles → umount B, every file sha-equal on A → umount A → `fsck --offline --scrub` 0 findings

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A LIVE MEMBER EVICTED AT T_OWNER UNDER THE DEAD MANAGER'S STRIPED HOT DIRECTORY (the flakes ledger's second shape, 2026-10-22) — A (the manager) holds `hot` striped over K = 64; B JOINED storms creates into it → kill -9 A ⇒ B PARKS at T_self → remount A (term 2) → B's reclaim lands in the grace window → B's member beat is HELD (SQUEEZEFS_TEST_MEMBERSHIP_BEAT_HOLD: no renewal, no reclaim beat, every other thread serving the storm) past T_owner ⇒ B's COMMITTERS park the gate at T_self on the member's own clock (its second park, with the beat still held: no commit past T_self), A evicts the silent B at T_owner (`tick — 1 evicted`) and recovers its region → released: the beat's reclaim meets the closed grace ⇒ UnknownLease ⇒ B holds acked bytes no layout names (64 KiB written through an fd a process holds open under the close write-back posture: write-side custody) ⇒ no re-join in place (decision 0003 §BS) ⇒ B POISONED (every volume FAILED, the move epoch closed) → the fail-stop: the storm's parked create and a fresh one answer EIO at once (never held), the storm child ends when told, `umount B` completes with the crash shape (no release, no page write; exit 1), A serves `hot` on (ls = find), no tripwire on A → fsck --offline --scrub 0 findings (red: a create held at the move gate for T_park_max per op, the storm child unkillable, the shard hung in wait4; B committed through the hold and its stop released 61 recovered slots: A's lookup wedged past the 51 s request timeout)

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A LIVE MEMBER EVICTED WITH NOTHING UN-LANDED RE-JOINS IN PLACE (charter §5.5, decision 0003 §BS; the owner's ruling (b), 2026-10-24) — A (the manager) mkdirs `shared`; B JOINED writes `own/f` (1 MiB, fsync'd) and a process holds it OPEN read-write; B goes idle-clean → B's member beat is HELD (SQUEEZEFS_TEST_MEMBERSHIP_BEAT_HOLD) past T_owner ⇒ A evicts the silent B at T_owner and recovers its region → released: B parks at T_self, its reclaim meets UnknownLease ⇒ B holds nothing un-landed (the ring's head = the head A's recovery read; no custody, no resident, no parked refinement, no intent) ⇒ B RE-JOINS IN PLACE under the same live FUSE mount (a fresh JoinAppender, a new membership epoch; no poison, no park expiry) → the held fds overwrite the file's head and APPEND 128 KiB after the re-join, a fresh open appends 128 KiB more, and B and A read `own/f` byte-equal; B's holder table keeps no grant over the retired slots (`dlm_token_outstanding` 0); B creates and renames in A's `shared`, both list the same; the predecessor's death record retires (the member is live again) and A's `scrub --online` leases a read shard to B's fleet worker: completed, 0 findings; no tripwire on either → umount B (exit 0: the successor's clean leave), umount A (exit 0) → fsck --offline --scrub 0 findings (red: UnknownLease poisoned B — every volume FAILED, EIO until remount; on 23db6c2 B's holder kept 2 grants over the retired slots; with the predecessor's death record standing, the scrub judged the live successor dead — C15)

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A LIVE MEMBER EVICTED WITH UN-LANDED STATE FAIL-STOPS (the re-join's negative arm, decision 0003 §BS) — B JOINED under the close write-back posture (SQUEEZEFS_WRITEBACK_POSTURE=close: custody lands at the close) writes 64 KiB into `own/g` through an fd a process holds OPEN (acked, never published: write-side custody) → B's beat is HELD past T_owner ⇒ A evicts B and recovers its region → released: UnknownLease ⇒ B holds acked bytes no layout names ⇒ NO re-join: B fail-stops exactly as before (the park's expiry, POISONED, every volume FAILED) — a fresh op answers EIO within the bound (no fork: the custody is never published under a successor), umount B (exit 1, the crash shape: nothing written), A serves on with no tripwire → fsck --offline --scrub 0 findings

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A LIVE MEMBER'S SLOW FOLLOW-UP NEVER COSTS ITS LEASE — THE DEAD MANAGER'S DOUBLE PARK UNDER LOAD (the kill matrix's second park, 2026-10-24) — A (the manager) holds `hot` striped over K = 64; B JOINED storms creates into it → kill -9 A ⇒ B PARKS at T_self → remount A (term 2) → B's reclaim lands in the grace window → B's FOLLOW-UP (its wire duties besides the renewal: the census pull, the re-point, the re-publication, the set-config learn) is HELD (SQUEEZEFS_TEST_MEMBERSHIP_FOLLOW_HOLD: a call to the freshly remounted manager slow past T_owner, what the gate's load did) while the storm goes on ⇒ B's renewals go on at their cadence through 2 × T_owner (the beat waits on nothing else): A evicts nobody, B never parks a second time, no UnknownLease, no poison → released: the follow-up completes, the storm ends, `ls` = `find` and the stat digest equal from A and B, no open intent → umount B (exit 0), A → fsck --offline --scrub 0 findings (red: the follow-up ran on the beat — B's committers parked the gate at T_self, A evicted the live B at T_owner, the reclaim met UnknownLease, B POISONED: the double park)

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A MEMBER JOINS A SET WHOSE MANAGER HAS REMOUNTED TWICE — format → A mounts and writes → umount, mount, write → umount, mount, write (three incarnations, three listeners) → B JOINS dialling the third → B reads every byte of all three and writes its own → umount B, A → `fsck --offline --scrub` 0 findings

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A MEMBER JOINS A SET WHOSE MANAGER HAS REMOUNTED — format → A (the manager) mounts and writes → `umount` A → A mounts again (a fresh ephemeral listener) and writes → B mounts and JOINS as appender 1, dialling A's LIVE listener (B's `manager_endpoint` is A's `wire_endpoint`) → B reads every byte A wrote and writes its own → umount B (A reads B's files) → umount A → `fsck --offline --scrub` 0 findings (red: B dialled the first incarnation's listener off tree 0's projection — `device I/O failed (IO, terminal)`)

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A MEMBER JOINS A SET WHOSE MANAGER WAS KILLED — format → A mounts and writes → umount → A as a `--daemon --supervise` daemon writes (inline files acked, never fsync'd) → `kill -9`: the supervisor replays the journal tail and releases the guard → A mounts again (every acked file whole) and writes → B JOINS dialling the successor's listener → B reads every byte and writes its own → umount B, A → `fsck --offline --scrub` 0 findings

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A MEMBER'S CACHED COPY OF ANOTHER MEMBER'S BLOCKS NEVER OUTLIVES THE BLOCKS' RE-USE (0003 §W.2) — two 192 MiB data volumes of 1 MiB blocks, no write cache (every write beyond inline striped) → mount A (the manager) + B JOINED (the dest lease off: its window reads are whole-block fills that deposit) → A writes `f` (two blocks, fsync'd) → A fills the set to ENOSPC → B reads `f` until its tiers hold its blocks → A `rm f`: the delete recalls B's token and B purges the blocks' keys before it acks (scoped purges ≥ 1, purged keys ≥ 2 on B; when B's token cache shed its entry, the shed purged them at the drop) → A writes `g` (two blocks, fsync'd) into the blocks the rm freed: B's tiers dropped `f`'s blocks before it landed → B reads `g`: sha-equal to A's, never `f`'s bytes

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A MOUNT THAT RACES THE PREVIOUS UNMOUNT WAITS, THEN SERVES (xfstests generic/604) — a `--daemon --supervise` mount, 501 staged 8 KiB files (never fsync'd) → `squeezefs umount` in the BACKGROUND and a second `--daemon --supervise` mount of the same set at once, the first daemon's dismount pass held on SQUEEZEFS_TEST_PROMOTION_HOLD (its mount already off the table, its writer lock held): the second mount meets the exiting holder's lock and WAITS — its log names the holder and why, it is alive and unmounted while the hold stands, never BUSY → released: the umount exits 0 (`clean unmount`, `exited (wait status 0x0)`), the second mount returns 0 within the orderly-exit ceiling as the set's MANAGER with `guard_exiting_holder_waits` ≥ 1, every file whole, exactly one daemon of the set alive, the supervisors silent → clean umount → `fsck --offline --scrub` 0 findings; the same cycle on a `--single-writer` set (the suites' posture) and on the SYMMETRIC default (where the join door must not be taken against an exiting manager) (red: `another writer holds the single-writer guard … (BUSY, refusal)` at once on the single-writer set — the release run's `-g auto` stopped at generic/604 — and `device I/O failed` from a join of the exiting manager on the symmetric one)

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A NO-OPEN CLOSE IS THE WRITE-BACK DRAIN (decision 0003 §AF) — format (no write cache: a partial block parks in RAM) → mount with SQUEEZEFS_FUSE_NO_OPEN=1 (the daemon latches the connection at ready: its own `.stats` open, the ONE OPEN answered ENOSYS) → `g` written and read → 1 MiB + 1000 B into a fresh `f` (a CREATE: no RELEASE will ever come) and appended to `g` (no OPEN at all) by plain redirections → kill -9 the moment the last close returned: nothing parked, nothing owed, no RELEASE, ≥ 2 FLUSH drains, ONE OPEN → fsck --offline clean → remount → both files whole

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A PUNCH, A ZERO RANGE AND A SAME-SIZE TRUNCATE SURVIVE A POWER CUT (fstests generic/695, 092; charter §6.6) — a set over device-mapper slices of 4 MiB blocks: generic/092's `falloc -k 0 12m` + `pwrite 0 5m` + `truncate 5m` returns the reservation past EOF (`df` 12 → 8 MiB) and `falloc -k 5m 5m` + `truncate 7m` keeps it (12 MiB); generic/695's `truncate 12M` + `pwrite -S 0xab 2M 8M` + sync, then `fpunch 2M 2M` + `fpunch 8M 2M` + fsync (and the same with `fzero`) reads zeros at [2M, 4M) and [8M, 10M) around the 0xab of [4M, 8M) → dm-flakey drops every write (the power cut) → unmount → the working table → fsck --offline --scrub clean → remount: every file byte-exact as fsync'd → clean unmount; no error line, no tripwire (red on dev: `fpunch 8M 2M` and `fzero 8M 2M` — a range starting ON a block boundary and ending inside it — zeroed nothing, read 0xab before and after the cut; the same-size truncate kept the reservation, `df` 12)

cli.smoke.test.smoke: A RE-JOIN WHOSE MEMBERSHIP JOIN IS REFUSED LEAVES ITS SUCCESSOR CLEANLY (decision 0003 §BS) — B JOINED idle-clean under SQUEEZEFS_TEST_REJOIN_MEMBER_REFUSED → its beat held past T_owner, A evicts and recovers it → released: B holds nothing un-landed, the successor joins (a new appender) but its membership join is refused ⇒ the successor closes UNPUBLISHED — the clean leave of a fresh join (rotor released, page Free) — and B fail-stops over the retired predecessor (EIO, exit 1 with nothing written) → after both unmounts no joiner's appender page is Live and only the predecessor's is Recovered (the successor's Free), fsck clean (red: the successor was published first, died with the mount and A recovered it too)
